translationRepairs: His elder brother Zhou Qiao was married to Emperor Gaozu's fourth daughter, Princess Dexian of Xuancheng.
His elder brother Zhou Qiao was married to Emperor Gaozu's fourth daughter, Princess De of Xuancheng.
宣城德公主 names the fief 宣城 and the epithet 德 only; Dexian invents a second graph not present in the title.

After the usurper Liu Shao murdered the emperor and seized the throne, Prince Liu Dan of Suizhou raised a loyal rising in Kuaiji; Shao promoted Qiao to General Who Conquers the Army, and Dan's call to arms reached him as well.

After the usurper Liu Shao murdered the emperor and seized the throne, Prince Liu Dan of Sui raised a loyal rising in Kuaiji; Shao promoted Qiao to General Who Conquers the Army, and Dan's call to arms reached him as well.
隨王 is the princely title Prince of Sui; Suizhou adds an unwritten 州.
When the rebel Shao assassinated and enthroned himself, Prince Suizhi Dan raised righteousness in Kuaiji; Shao gave Qiao the title General Who Conquers the Army, and Dan's proclamation also arrived.

When the rebel Shao assassinated and enthroned himself, Prince of Sui, Dan, raised righteousness in Kuaiji; Shao gave Qiao the title General Who Conquers the Army, and Dan's proclamation also arrived.
隨王誕 is the title 隨王 plus the given name 誕; Suizhi fuses title and name into a false personal name.

He first served as Acting Staff Officer under the Champion General of the Prince of Nanping, Shi, then as Gentlemen Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Secretary of the Minister of Education; for requesting leave on urgent grounds without awaiting approval he was removed from the register.

He first served as Acting Staff Officer under the Champion General of the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, then as Gentlemen Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Secretary of the Minister of Education; for requesting leave on urgent grounds without awaiting approval he was removed from the register.
南平王鑠 is Liu Shuo; 鑠 is shuò, not Shi, and the idiomatic line already has Shuo.
In Han's middle years they could serve the barbarians because horses were many; afterward the barbarians submitted to Han also because horses were few.
In Han's middle years they could deal with the barbarians because horses were many; afterward the barbarians submitted to Han also because horses were few.
能事胡者 contrasts with 胡之後服漢者: Han could handle the Hu because it had many horses, not serve them; 事 here is manage or cope with.
Even if the emperor were reduced to gathering soap or the empress to plain cloth, that would be unworthy.
Even if the emperor were reduced to the shabbiness of coarse black cloth, or the empress to plain cloth, that would be unworthy.
集皁之陋 is paired with 帛布之鄙 as extreme frugality in dress; 皁 is coarse black or menial cloth, not soap.
Gold souls, green jade, brocade and fine silk gauze, strange colors and unusual patterns—common people may not wear them, and those above may not bestow them.
Gold foil and green jade, brocade and fine silk gauze, strange colors and unusual patterns—common people may not wear them, and those above may not bestow them.
金魄翠玉 lists luxury ornaments; 魄 here is foil or amber, not souls.

One ought to cause those the age calls masters of classics and history, skilled in rhetoric and calculation, capable in administration and strategy, and those of partial arts and small ways, to tie hunting caps and kneel perilously, broadly seeking their employment.

One ought to cause those the age calls masters of classics and history, skilled in rhetoric and calculation, capable in administration and strategy, and those of partial arts and small ways, to adjust their cap-strings and kneel in audience, broadly seeking their employment.
獵纓危膝 is the court-audience gesture of gathering cap-strings and kneeling upright, not hunting caps or perilous kneeling.
Since the Buddhist teaching spread, its source has been deep; profound inspection and fine measurement show it is not deep after all.
Since the Buddhist teaching spread, it has had a source; profound inspection and fine measurement show it is not deep after all.
其來有源 says the teaching has an origin; 深 belongs only to the following denial 固非深矣, so calling the source deep is an invented contradiction.
His grandfather Ji was Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
His grandfather Ji was Chamberlain of the Palace Guard of the Jin.
晉光祿勳 is the Jin Guanglu xun, Chamberlain of the Palace Guard; it is not 尚書令 or another secretariat directorship, and 晉 must be kept.
His grandfather Ji was Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
His grandfather Ji was Guanglu xun (Chamberlain of the Palace Guard) of the Jin.
The literal line repeats the same false office; 晉光祿勳 is Guanglu xun of the Jin, not Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

If one should be re-ordained, then order him first to study righteous conduct and examine his inner spirit; only if he can with certainty transform grass and rot heaven and human affairs and rouse his essence to go forward—even the son of a marquis or king should not be detained.

If someone should be ordained anew, then order him first to study righteous conduct and ground it in his inner spirit; only if he can surely let the body decay like grass, put aside the human and heavenly realm, and rouse his essence to go forward—even a son of a marquis or king should not be held back.
草腐人天 is Buddhist world-renunciation, treating the body as rotting grass and leaving the human and heavenly realms, not transforming grass or rotting heaven and human affairs.

At the time those imprisoned were very numerous, cases often lasting years; when Huaiwen took office he tried cases in five commanderies totaling nine hundred thirty-six prisons, and all praised his fairness.

At the time those imprisoned were very numerous, cases often lasting years; when Huaiwen took office he tried cases in five commanderies totaling nine hundred thirty-six cases, and all praised his fairness.
訊五郡九百三十六獄 counts 936 judicial cases heard across five commanderies, not 936 prisons.
